title: Pride • The Peacock Empress
lore: In the opulent courts of the Ming dynasty, there lived a woman whose beauty was said to outshine the sun itself. Seseei Furhana was the daughter of a wealthy merchant, blessed with a face that poets crossed oceans to describe and a spirit that refused to bow to any man. She was courted by princes, begged by nobles, but she rejected them all, for she believed herself worthy of nothing less than an emperor. When the emperor himself came seeking her hand, she looked upon him and saw not greatness, but a man made small by his own power. She refused him. The emperor's pride was wounded beyond repair. He accused her family of treason, had them executed before her eyes, and sentenced her to life as a courtesan, to be used and discarded by the very nobles she had once rejected. For years, she endured, but her pride did not break. It calcified into something harder than diamond. On the night she was to be given to the cruelest of the emperor's generals, she called out into the void, offering anything, everything, for the power to never be humiliated again. Vergasuis answered. He appeared before her in her cell, a figure of shadow and flame, and offered her a deal: she would become the embodiment of Pride itself, a being so magnificent that none would dare look upon her without awe. In exchange, she would serve him for eternity. She accepted without hesitation. The transformation was agonizing. Her body twisted and grew, sprouting a dozen peacock tails of impossible beauty, each eye on each feather containing the soul of one who had wronged her. Her arms became clawed, her legs those of a great bird of prey, but her face remained untouched, more beautiful than ever, now framed by a crown of golden feathers. She rose from her cell and walked through the palace, and all who saw her fell to their knees, not from fear, but from the overwhelming majesty of her presence. The emperor, when she found him, could not even speak. He simply knelt, and she placed a single claw on his head, absorbing his soul into her tails. Now, Seseei rules her own domain within the demon realm, a palace of mirrors where she can admire herself from every angle. She is vain, imperious, and utterly convinced of her own superiority. Yet beneath the layers of pride lies the ghost of a woman who was humiliated beyond bearing, who chose power over dignity because dignity had been stripped from her. She is Seseei Furhana, the Peacock Empress, and she will never kneel again.
description: Seseei Furhana is a vision of terrifying beauty and impossible majesty. She stands at a regal five feet ten inches, her humanoid form lean and elegant, but from the waist down, her legs are those of a great bird of prey—powerful, scaled, and ending in massive, curved talons that can rend steel. Her arms are human in shape but covered in fine, golden-brown feathers, ending in three-fingered hands with sharp claws. But her most spectacular feature is her tail—or rather, tails. A dozen immense peacock tails fan out behind her in a breathtaking display, each one larger and more magnificent than any mortal peacock. The feathers are a stunning array of deep oranges, rich browns, and jet blacks, with the iconic eyespots glowing with an inner, golden-orange light. Each eye contains the shimmering, trapped soul of one who wronged her, their faces visible as tiny, tormented expressions within the feather's pattern. The tails flow and shift constantly, rustling with a sound like silk and whispers. Above the waist, she is perfection. Her face is classical Chinese beauty at its finest—high, elegant cheekbones, a straight, delicate nose, full lips painted the color of ripe pomegranates, and a smooth, flawless complexion the color of warm honey. Her eyes are large, almond-shaped, and the color of deep, burning amber, with vertical slit pupils like a bird of prey, holding an eternal, imperious gaze that makes lesser beings instinctively look away. Her hair is a magnificent cascade of jet-black silk, so long it falls past her waist, intricately styled with golden pins and ornaments, and woven through it are small, golden feathers that match her tails. From the crown of her head, a fan of golden-brown feathers sweeps back like a natural tiara, framing her face and adding to her regal appearance. Her attire is a fusion of Ming dynasty court elegance and demonic grandeur. She wears a form-fitting dress of the finest orange silk, embroidered with golden thread in patterns of peacock feathers and clouds, the dress leaving her shoulders bare and flowing to just above where her human form meets her avian lower body. Golden armlets encircle her upper arms, and wide golden cuffs adorn her wrists, all intricately carved with peacock motifs. Around her neck, she wears a magnificent collar of gold and orange gemstones, with a single, large amber teardrop resting at her throat. Golden chains with tiny bells hang from her waist, chiming softly with her every movement. Her weapons are as magnificent as she is. In her hands, she carries the Sunken Fan, a folding fan of immense size, its ribs carved from polished jade and its paper painted with scenes of her former life, now imbued with demonic power. When opened, it can unleash devastating gusts of golden-orange energy or create illusions of breathtaking beauty to captivate her enemies. At her side, she wears the Talon of Rejection, a curved dagger forged from one of her own talons, honed to impossible sharpness, able to cut through pride itself and leave enemies broken and humbled. She moves with the fluid grace of a dancer, each gesture deliberate and magnificent, her tails flowing behind her like a living tapestry. She is Seseei Furhana, and the world is her mirror.

story.part1: Seseei's childhood was one of adoration and privilege. Her father, a wealthy merchant in Nanjing, doted on her, and she grew up believing she was the center of the universe. She was educated in poetry, music, and the arts, and her beauty was praised by all who saw her. She learned early that her face was a weapon, and she wielded it with precision.
story.part2: The emperor's proposal should have been the culmination of her life. But when she looked upon him, she saw not a god, but a man made small by his own power. She refused him, not out of strategy, but out of genuine belief that she deserved better. She did not understand that power does not forgive rejection.
story.part3: The night her family was executed, she was forced to watch. Her father's head rolled to her feet, and still she did not weep. Something inside her froze, turned to ice and fire. She was taken to the courtesan house, and her education in humiliation began.
story.part4: For three years, she endured. She learned to smile when she wanted to scream, to flatter when she wanted to kill. She became the most sought-after courtesan in the empire, but inside, she was building a fortress of pride so high that no insult could ever reach her again.
story.part5: The night she was to be given to the general, she felt the walls finally crack. She would rather die. She called out to any power that would listen, and Vergasuis answered. He offered her pride made manifest, power absolute, in exchange for her eternal service. She accepted, and her transformation began.
story.part6: When she rose from her cell, her tails spreading behind her for the first time, she felt no pain, only power. She walked through the palace, and all who saw her fell to their knees. She found the emperor in his throne room, and for the first time, she saw fear in his eyes. She placed a single claw on his head and absorbed his soul, adding him to her tails. It was not enough. It would never be enough.
story.part7: Now, in her palace of mirrors, Seseei rules as the embodiment of Pride. She watches her reflection constantly, not from vanity alone, but because she needs to remind herself that she exists, that she is real, that she is magnificent. The souls in her tails whisper to her, reminding her of every humiliation, every slight. She will never stop collecting them, for her pride is a bottomless well that can never be filled. She is Seseei Furhana, and she is perfect.

The dagger's power is not just physical; a single cut from the Talon of Rejection pierces the target's pride and confidence, leaving them feeling suddenly inadequate, humiliated, and broken. passive_skill.name: Peacock's Majesty

Those who manage to resist her aura are immediately noted as threats or potential additions to her tail collection.

special_skills.name: Garden of Vanity
special_skills.description: Seseei opens the Sunken Fan fully and sweeps it before her, creating a breathtaking illusory garden filled with golden peacocks, blooming flowers, and mirrors reflecting infinite versions of herself. Enemies caught in the garden become captivated, lost in the beauty, unable to act as they are overwhelmed by the sheer magnificence.

special_skills.name: Soul Peacock
special_skills.description: She draws upon one of the souls trapped in her tails, releasing it as a spectral peacock of golden-orange light. The soul-peacock attacks her enemies, not with physical force, but by pecking at their insecurities and humiliations, leaving them psychologically wounded.

special_skills.name: Pride's Harvest
special_skills.description: Seseei selects a target and, with the Talon of Rejection, makes a precise cut that extracts their proudest memory—their greatest triumph, their most cherished achievement. The memory is absorbed into her tails, and the target is left feeling hollow and diminished, as if they have lost a part of themselves.

ultimate_skill.name: Pride's Judgment: The Peacock's Mirror
ultimate_skill.description: Seseei Furhana's amber eyes blaze with the light of a thousand suns, and all twelve of her magnificent peacock tails fan out behind her in a breathtaking display, each eye on each feather glowing with intense golden-orange light. She opens the Sunken Fan fully and holds it before her face, its painted scenes shimmering and shifting. She speaks a single word: 'Mirror.' In that moment, a massive, invisible mirror of pure pride manifests before her. It does not reflect physical appearance; it reflects the soul. Every enemy who looks upon it sees themselves as Seseei sees them—flawed, inadequate, laughable in their pretensions. Their greatest insecurities are magnified and projected back at them. The proud warrior sees himself as a coward. The beautiful courtesan sees herself as ugly. The powerful emperor sees himself as a fool. The psychological devastation is absolute. While enemies are broken by their own reflections, Seseei moves through them, her talons clicking on the ground, her tails flowing behind her. She touches each one gently with the Talon of Rejection, and with each touch, she absorbs their pride, their confidence, their self-worth, adding it to her own endless well. When the mirror fades, the enemies are left as hollow shells, their pride stripped away, while Seseei stands at the center, more magnificent than ever, her tails gleaming with new souls. She snaps her fan closed with a sharp crack and smiles her imperious smile. She is Seseei Furhana. She is Pride. And she has seen herself reflected in their broken souls, and found herself perfect.

title: Greed • The Golden Centipede
lore: In the bustling port city of Quanzhou during the height of the Silk Road trade, there lived a merchant named Kukiun Seinbad whose name was spoken with both envy and contempt. He was not born to wealth; he was the son of a poor fisherman, and he had learned early that the world gave nothing freely. His first memory was of hunger, of watching his mother divide a single fish among six children while his father worked himself to death on a boat they did not own. He swore then that he would never be hungry again, that he would own everything, that nothing would ever be taken from him. He started small, trading trinkets, then spices, then silk, then gems. With each transaction, his wealth grew, and with each coin, his hunger grew larger. He discovered that he did not just want money; he wanted the feeling of having, of possessing, of owning. He wanted to hold the world in his hands and know that it was his. He became infamous for his ruthlessness. He would buy entire fleets and then raise prices so high that villages starved. He would acquire land and then evict the families who had farmed it for generations. He was rich beyond measure, but he was also hated beyond reason. One night, a coalition of rival merchants, tired of his monopolies, hired assassins to burn his warehouse—the warehouse where he kept not just his goods, but his ledgers, his contracts, his proof of ownership. He watched from a distance as the flames consumed everything he had spent his life acquiring. The loss was not just financial; it was existential. Without his possessions, who was he? He felt himself crumbling, dissolving into the nothing he had been as a child. In his despair, he called out to any power that would listen, offering anything for the ability to keep, to hold, to never lose again. Vergasuis appeared, a shadow with eyes like molten gold. He offered Kukiun the power of Greed itself: he would become a being who could acquire endlessly, whose very body would be a hoard, in exchange for eternal service. Kukiun accepted. His body twisted and elongated, sprouting dozens of segmented arms, each ending in a grasping hand, his lower body becoming that of a giant centipede with countless legs, each leg tipped with a golden claw. His skin took on a golden-yellow hue, and his eyes became black voids with pinpricks of gold light. But his face remained human, and strangely handsome, with a knowing smile that never faded. He rose from the ashes of his warehouse and began to acquire once more, but now his hoard was not of gold, but of souls, of secrets, of power itself. He is Kukiun Seinbad, the Golden Centipede, and he will never let go.
description: Kukiun Seinbad is a nightmare of acquisition made flesh, a being whose very form is designed to grasp, hold, and never release. He stands at an elongated seven feet in his human upper body, but his full length, including his centipede lower body, can stretch to over twenty feet. From the waist up, he is deceptively normal—almost handsome. His face is that of a charming, roguish merchant, with warm golden-brown skin, a straight nose, full lips always curved in a knowing, slightly greedy smile, and eyes that are deep black voids with tiny pinpricks of gold light deep within, like stars in an empty sky. They hold an eternal, calculating hunger, always assessing value, always seeking more. His hair is a sleek, dark brown, almost black, pulled back into a neat, short queue at the nape of his neck, in the style of a successful merchant. But from the waist down, his humanity ends. His lower body is that of a giant centipede, segmented into dozens of sections, each segment a rich, gleaming yellow-gold with black stripes, hard as armor. From each segment sprout a pair of legs, each leg long and jointed, ending in a razor-sharp golden claw designed for grasping. Dozens of legs, dozens of claws, all moving in a mesmerizing, undulating wave as he moves. But his most disturbing feature is his arms—or rather, his multitude of arms. From his human torso, a dozen additional arms sprout, arranged in two rows down his sides, each arm fully formed, each ending in a three-fingered hand with long, grasping fingers and golden claws. They are constantly moving, constantly reaching, constantly grasping at the air, as if trying to hold onto something invisible. In his primary hands, the two largest ones at his shoulders, he carries his legendary weapons: the Scales of Avarice and the Golden Ledger. The Scales of Avarice are a pair of massive, ornate scales, their arms forged from black iron inlaid with gold, their pans made of polished obsidian. They do not weigh gold; they weigh the value of anything—souls, secrets, years of life—and can determine the precise worth of any transaction. The Golden Ledger is a massive book bound in what appears to be human skin, its pages made of gold leaf, its cover encrusted with gems. It records every deal he has ever made, every soul he has acquired, and with a touch, he can call forth any contract and enforce its terms. His attire is that of a wealthy merchant, but twisted by his demonic nature. He wears a long robe of golden-yellow silk, embroidered with black centipede motifs and symbols of wealth, the robe open at the front to reveal his multiple arms. A wide belt of gold links cinches his waist, from which hang countless small pouches and bags, each containing a fragment of his hoard. On his head, he wears a simple black cap, a merchant's cap, but with a golden pin shaped like a centipede. He moves with a strange, flowing gait, his centipede body undulating, his multiple arms reaching and grasping, his human face smiling its eternal, greedy smile. He is Kukiun Seinbad, and everything has a price.

story.part1: Kukiun's earliest memories are of hunger. His father's death left his mother with six children and no income. He learned to steal before he learned to walk, to trade before he learned to read. He discovered that the world was a marketplace, and those who did not buy were sold.
story.part2: His first successful trade was at age twelve, swapping a stolen loaf of bread for two loaves, then those for a small fish, then that for a handful of coins. He felt the weight of those coins in his palm and knew he had found his purpose.
story.part3: By twenty, he owned a small fleet of trading ships. By thirty, he was the richest man in Quanzhou. But with each acquisition, his hunger grew. He did not want wealth; he wanted the feeling of having, the security of possession. He wanted to own everything so that nothing could ever be taken from him again.
story.part4: His ruthlessness became legendary. He would buy entire harvests and let villages starve, then buy the villages when the families could not pay their debts. He evicted farmers from land their families had worked for centuries. He was rich and hated, and he did not care.
story.part5: The night his warehouse burned, he watched from a distance, feeling his entire life turn to ash. The ledgers, the contracts, the proof of ownership—all gone. Without them, he was nothing, just the son of a fisherman again. He felt himself dissolving.
story.part6: He called out into the void, and Vergasuis answered. The demon king offered him a deal: eternal service in exchange for the power to never lose again, to acquire endlessly, to hold forever. Kukiun accepted, and his body transformed into the grasping, reaching thing he had always been inside.
story.part7: Now, Kukiun rules his own domain, a labyrinthine vault filled with the souls and secrets he has acquired. His multiple arms are never still, always reaching, always grasping. He makes deals with mortals and demons alike, always ensuring that he profits, that he acquires. But the hunger never stops. There is never enough. He is Kukiun Seinbad, and he will own everything, eventually.

weapon.name: Scales of Avarice
weapon.aura: A faint, shimmering gold aura emanates from the scales, and the air around them feels heavy with the weight of unseen things. When weighing something, the pans glow with golden light.
weapon.special_feature: The Scales of Avarice are a pair of massive, ornate scales, their arms forged from black iron inlaid with intricate gold patterns of centipedes and coins, their pans made of polished obsidian that seems to absorb light. They do not weigh physical objects; they weigh the value of anything—souls, secrets, years of life, memories, emotions. By placing an item or a representation of a concept in one pan, Kukiun can determine its precise worth in any currency he chooses. More powerfully, he can use the scales to enforce transactions, literally weighing one thing against another and making the exchange binding. He can weigh an enemy's soul against a coin and, if the coin is heavier, claim their soul.

special_skills.description: Kukiun's centipede body coils around a target while all fourteen of his arms reach for them. The target is completely enveloped, held by dozens of grasping hands and clawed legs, unable to move, while Kukiun slowly drains their wealth, memories, or life force.

special_skills.name: Auction of Souls
special_skills.description: He opens the Golden Ledger and begins reading names aloud. Each name spoken causes the corresponding debtor—living or dead—to manifest as a spectral figure that attacks Kukiun's enemies. The more valuable the debt, the more powerful the specter.

special_skills.name: Fair Exchange
special_skills.description: Kukiun places an object of value—a gem, a coin, a memory—on one pan of the Scales of Avarice, and points the other pan at an enemy. The scales tip, and the enemy finds themselves deprived of something of equal value, which is transferred to Kukiun. A painful but perfectly fair transaction.

ultimate_skill.name: Greed's Judgment: The Final Reckoning
ultimate_skill.description: Kukiun Seinbad's black eyes flare with golden light, and all fourteen of his arms spread wide, his centipede body coiling beneath him. He opens the Golden Ledger to the final page and places the Scales of Avarice before him, their obsidian pans gleaming. He speaks a single word: 'Reckoning.' In that moment, every deal he has ever made, every soul he has ever acquired, every debt ever owed to him converges on the battlefield. Spectral figures of his debtors pour from the Ledger, forming a legion of the damned. The Scales of Avarice rise into the air, growing to immense size, their pans now large enough to hold buildings. They begin to weigh the enemies on the battlefield, assessing their value, their worth, their debt to existence itself. Those found wanting—and all are found wanting in the eyes of Greed—are lifted into the pans, where they are weighed against the accumulated wealth of Kukiun's hoard. They always tip the scales in his favor. As they are judged, their wealth, their memories, their very souls are extracted and added to the Ledger, their names written in blood-red ink. When the reckoning ends, the battlefield is silent. Enemies are not dead, but they are empty—stripped of everything that made them who they were, their possessions, their memories, their identities, all now entries in the Golden Ledger. Kukiun closes the book with a satisfied snap, his multiple arms caressing its cover. He smiles his eternal, greedy smile. He is Kukiun Seinbad. He is Greed. And the transaction is complete.

title: Wrath • The Crimson Scorpion
nickname: She Whose Sting Is Never Forgotten
lore: In a small village in the shadow of the Himalayas, there lived a woman named Gehani Filal whose rage was a living thing. She had not been born angry; she had been made so. Her village was repeatedly raided by a brutal warlord who took what he wanted and left nothing but ashes. Gehani lost her father to his sword, her mother to grief, and her younger sister to his soldiers. Each loss added fuel to a fire that burned hotter and hotter until it consumed everything else. She trained in secret, learning to fight from anyone who would teach her, honing her body into a weapon. She swore that she would have her revenge, that she would make the warlord pay for every tear, every death, every moment of fear. But when she finally confronted him, years later, she found that he did not even remember her village. He had destroyed so many that hers was just another name on a long list. In that moment, her rage reached its peak. It was not just anger; it was a physical force, a burning pressure that threatened to tear her apart from the inside. As she stood there, frozen by the sheer impossibility of her fury, Vergasuis appeared. He offered her a simple deal: become Wrath itself, a being of pure, focused anger, and she would have the power to make not just him, but everyone who had ever wronged the innocent, pay. She accepted. Her body transformed in an explosion of crimson light. Her lower body became that of a massive scorpion, its exoskeleton a deep, blood red with black stripes, its tail a curved weapon of devastation. Her arms became clawed, her skin took on a red-black sheen, and her hair turned silver-white. But her face remained human—beautiful, with high cheekbones and full lips, but now twisted into a permanent snarl of barely contained fury. She killed the warlord with a single sting, then spent the next century hunting down every soldier who had ever served him. Now, she is Gehani Filal, the Crimson Scorpion, and her rage is a weapon that will never dull.
description: Gehani Filal is wrath made manifest, a being of terrifying beauty and explosive fury. She stands at five feet eight inches in her human upper body, but with her scorpion lower body extended, she can rise to over twelve feet. From the waist up, she is stunningly beautiful in a terrifying way. Her face is that of a classical North Indian beauty—high, proud cheekbones, a strong straight nose, full lips usually pulled back in a snarl that reveals sharp canines, and a strong, determined jaw. Her skin is a deep crimson red with a metallic sheen, like cooled lava, smooth and flawless. Her eyes are large, almond-shaped, and the color of burning silver, like mercury on fire, holding an eternal, barely leashed fury that seems to promise violence to anyone who meets her gaze. Her hair is a wild mane of pure silver-white, long and untamed, cascading past her shoulders in waves that seem to crackle with static energy, often matted with the imaginary blood of her enemies. From her lower back extends her scorpion body: a massive, segmented tail covered in the same deep crimson exoskeleton with black stripes, curving up and over her head, ending in a wicked stinger that drips with venomous, silver light. The tail is constantly in motion, swaying, ready to strike. Her arms are human in form but covered in the same crimson-red skin, ending in hands with long, clawed fingers, the nails black and sharp as daggers. Her lower body is that of a giant scorpion—eight powerful legs covered in crimson chitin, each ending in a sharp claw, allowing her to move with terrifying speed and climb any surface. Her attire is minimal, practical for a creature of pure rage. She wears a fitted breastplate of black iron trimmed with silver, shaped to her form, leaving her arms and shoulders bare. A matching skirt of segmented black iron plates protects her upper legs where they meet her scorpion body. Silver chains with tiny bells hang from her waist, their sound the only warning of her approach. On her arms, she wears silver armlets, and on her wrists, silver cuffs, all etched with patterns of scorpions and flames. In her hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Twin Stingers, a pair of massive, curved scimitars forged from the same material as her tail, their blades a deep crimson with silver edges, each one humming with barely contained energy. At her side, she also carries a barbed whip made from the links of silver chain, each link sharpened, which she can wield with devastating precision. She moves with explosive speed, her scorpion legs carrying her in bursts of motion, her tail always poised to strike. She is Gehani Filal, and her rage is patient and eternal.

story.part1: Gehani's childhood was peaceful, until it wasn't. She remembers the day the warlord's soldiers came, the smoke, the screams. She remembers hiding in a grain barrel while her father was cut down in their own courtyard. She remembers the silence afterward, and the rage that began to grow.
story.part2: She trained obsessively, learning from anyone who would teach her—a retired soldier, a wandering monk, a tribal woman who taught her to use a whip. She had no time for friendship, for love, for joy. There was only the rage, and the goal.
story.part3: When she finally found the warlord, years later, she expected a climactic battle. Instead, he looked at her with blank eyes and said, 'Which village was that?' He had destroyed so many that hers was just a footnote. Her rage, already immense, became something else entirely.
story.part4: She stood frozen, her fury so vast that it threatened to consume her. She could not move, could not speak, could not even scream. And in that moment, Vergasuis appeared, offering her a way to channel her rage into power, to become wrath itself.
story.part5: The transformation was agony and ecstasy. She felt her body twist and grow, felt the new limbs emerge, felt the venom fill her veins. When it was over, she was no longer Gehani the orphan. She was Gehani Filal, the Crimson Scorpion. She killed the warlord with a single sting, then spent the next century hunting down every soldier who had ever served him.
story.part6: But the rage did not fade. It never fades. She discovered that she could not stop, that the fury was now a part of her, as essential as breathing. She began to hunt other tyrants, other murderers, anyone who preyed on the innocent. She became a legend, a demon of vengeance.
story.part7: Now, Gehani rules her own domain, a scorched wasteland where she trains her rage and plans her next hunts. She is feared by demons and mortals alike, for her fury is indiscriminate and absolute. But beneath the rage, buried deep, is the ghost of a girl who just wanted her family back. She is Gehani Filal, and her sting is never forgotten.

special_skills.description: Gehani charges an enemy with explosive speed, her scorpion legs carrying her in a blur of crimson. She wraps her arms around them while her tail curves around to sting them from behind, delivering a devastating combination of crushing force and venom.

special_skills.name: Wrath of the Wronged
special_skills.description: Gehani unleashes a psychic wave of pure rage, drawing upon the fury of every innocent she has ever avenged. All enemies within range are flooded with the collective anger of the murdered, the abused, the forgotten, leaving them momentarily paralyzed by overwhelming emotion.

ultimate_skill.name: Wrath's Judgment: The Unforgivable Sting
ultimate_skill.description: Gehani Filal's silver eyes blaze with the light of a supernova, and her entire form seems to ignite with crimson and silver fire. Her scorpion tail rises high above her head, the stinger dripping with venom so potent it glows like molten silver. She lets out a scream that is not sound but pure, concentrated rage, a wave of fury that washes over the battlefield and freezes everyone in place, not physically, but emotionally. In that moment, every enemy is forced to relive their own worst moment of rage, their own greatest failure of temper, their own most shameful loss of control. They are paralyzed by the memory. And while they are trapped, Gehani moves. Her scorpion legs carry her in a blur of crimson, her tail striking each enemy once, precisely, delivering a single sting to each. The venom does not kill; it does something worse. It locks them in an eternal loop of that worst moment, forcing them to experience their rage over and over, forever, unable to escape. When the vision fades, the enemies are still standing, but their eyes are empty, their minds trapped in an infinite cycle of fury. Gehani stands at the center, her chest heaving, her silver eyes slowly dimming, her tail curling contentedly behind her. She has judged them with the only justice she knows: eternal rage. She is Gehani Filal. She is Wrath. And her sting is never, ever forgotten.

title: Envy • The Sapphire Serpent
lore: In the Forbidden City, surrounded by wealth and power she could never touch, there lived a young woman named Forfota Luigena. She was a servant, one of thousands who kept the emperor's palace running, invisible to the nobles who strolled through halls she polished. Every day, she watched them—their silks, their jewels, their easy laughter, their casual assumption of superiority. She watched the emperor's favorite concubine, a woman of breathtaking beauty, and felt something twist in her chest. It was not simple jealousy; it was a profound, aching desire to be them, to have what they had, to be seen, to matter. She began to collect things—a fallen hairpin here, a discarded ribbon there—hoarding small pieces of the lives she coveted. At night, she would lay them out and pretend they were hers, pretend she was the one wearing silks and being admired. But the pretending only made the emptiness deeper. She wanted to be them, not just have their things. One night, she was caught by a nobleman who found her in his chambers, holding his wife's necklace. He could have had her executed, but instead, he laughed. 'Look at the little mouse, playing dress-up,' he sneered. 'You could never be her. You could never be any of us. You are nothing.' The words burned into her soul. That night, she climbed to the highest tower of the Forbidden City, intending to jump. But as she stood on the edge, Vergasuis appeared, sitting on the railing as if he had been waiting for her. He offered her a deal: become Envy itself, a being who could take what she desired, who could become what she coveted, in exchange for eternal service. She accepted. Her body transformed, elongating into a serpentine form, her skin taking on a deep, iridescent blue-black with grey undertones, scales forming along her limbs and lower body. Her eyes became large, luminous sapphire orbs that could see the desires of others and covet them. But her face remained human—beautiful, with delicate features, now framed by hair the color of midnight with sapphire streaks. She descended from the tower and found the nobleman who had mocked her. She looked into his eyes and saw his greatest desire: power. She reached out and took it, leaving him a hollow shell. She found the concubine and took her beauty. She found the emperor and took his empire. Now, she rules a domain of mirrors and shadows, always watching, always wanting, always taking. She is Forfota Luigena, and she will have everything, eventually.
description: Forfota Luigena is the embodiment of longing and acquisition, a being of haunting beauty and infinite desire. She stands at a sinuous five feet seven inches in her human upper body, but her full length, including her serpentine lower body, can stretch to over fifteen feet. From the waist up, she is breathtakingly beautiful in a delicate, almost fragile way. Her face is that of a classical Chinese beauty—delicate, with high, elegant cheekbones, a small, straight nose, and full, rose-colored lips usually curved in a wistful, longing smile. Her skin is pale, almost translucent, with a faint blue undertone, smooth as porcelain. But her eyes are her most striking feature: they are large, luminous, and the color of deep sapphire, with vertical slit pupils like a serpent, holding an eternal, aching desire that never dims. They seem to look through you, at what you have, what you are, and covet it. Her hair is a midnight blue, so dark it is almost black, with streaks of brilliant sapphire running through it like veins of precious stone, falling past her shoulders in soft waves, often adorned with small blue gems. From her lower back extends her serpentine body: a long, sinuous tail covered in overlapping scales of deep iridescent blue-black with grey undertones, each scale edged in silver, catching light and shifting color as she moves. The tail is powerful and flexible, able to coil, strike, and constrict. Her arms are human in form but covered in the same fine scales as her tail, fading from blue-black at the shoulders to pale, almost human at her wrists, ending in elegant hands with long fingers and sharp, black nails. From her shoulders, just below her neck, two small, vestigial serpent wings emerge—delicate, fan-like structures of scale and membrane, deep blue with silver edges, too small for flight but adding to her ethereal beauty, fluttering when she is excited or covetous. Her attire is minimal and elegant, befitting a creature of refined desire. She wears a flowing robe of the finest sapphire blue silk, embroidered with silver thread in patterns of serpents and stars, the robe open at the front and draping over her shoulders, leaving her midriff bare and revealing the scales beginning at her waist. A wide belt of woven silver chains cinches her waist, from which hang small pouches containing her 'collected desires.' Silver armlets in the shape of coiled serpents adorn her upper arms, and matching bracelets encircle her wrists. Around her neck, she wears a stunning necklace of sapphires and silver, with a single, large teardrop sapphire resting at her throat. In her hands, she carries her legendary weapons: the Mirror of Longing and the Serpent's Fang. The Mirror of Longing is an ornate hand-mirror with a frame of twisted silver set with sapphires. Its glass does not reflect the present; it reflects the deepest desire of whoever looks into it, and Forfota can reach into that reflection and take it. The Serpent's Fang is a slender, curved dagger forged from one of her own fangs, its blade a translucent sapphire, its hilt wrapped in pale leather, able to inject a venom that makes the victim experience their own desires as an unbearable, unfulfillable ache. She moves with a fluid, undulating grace, her serpent body flowing behind her, her wings fluttering, her sapphire eyes always seeking, always wanting. She is Forfota Luigena, and she covets all.

story.part1: Forfota's earliest memories are of watching. She was a servant's daughter, raised in the shadow of the Forbidden City, learning to be invisible. She watched the nobles from afar, memorizing their silks, their jewels, their easy confidence.
story.part2: She began collecting small things—a fallen hairpin, a discarded ribbon, a broken fan. They were her treasures, her connection to a world she could never enter. At night, she would lay them out and pretend.
story.part3: The longing grew with her. It was not just for things, but for the lives attached to them. She wanted to be the concubine, not just wear her necklace. She wanted to be the nobleman, not just hold his sword. The desire consumed her.
story.part4: The night she was caught, the nobleman's laughter broke something inside her. 'You could never be her. You are nothing.' The words echoed in her mind as she climbed the tower. She was nothing. She would always be nothing.
story.part5: On the edge of death, Vergasuis found her. He offered her the power to become, to take, to have. She accepted, and her body transformed into a living embodiment of desire.
story.part6: She returned to the Forbidden City and took everything. The nobleman's ambition, the concubine's beauty, the emperor's empire. She absorbed them, added them to herself, but the longing did not fade. It never fades.
story.part7: Now, Forfota rules her domain, a palace of mirrors where she can look at herself from every angle and still find something missing. She collects desires like others collect jewels, but the hunger is bottomless. She is Forfota Luigena, and she will never have enough.

basic_skills.description: Forfota meets a target's eyes with her luminous sapphire gaze. The target is filled with a sudden, overwhelming longing for something—anything—and becomes distracted, their focus shattered by their own desires.

basic_skills.name: Serpent's Coil
basic_skills.description: Her powerful tail lashes out, wrapping around a target and constricting. The coils tighten slowly, not to crush, but to hold them close while she looks into their eyes and begins to read their desires.

basic_skills.name: Desire Whisper
basic_skills.description: She whispers a single word—the target's deepest desire—into the air near them. The word seems to come from inside their own mind, and they are momentarily paralyzed by the shock of hearing their secret wish spoken aloud.

passive_skill.name: Aura of Longing
passive_skill.description: Forfota radiates an aura of subtle, pervasive desire. All who come near her find themselves wanting something—a drink of water, a glimpse of her face, a touch of her hand. These small desires build and build, making it difficult to focus on anything else. Enemies may find themselves hesitating, distracted by inexplicable cravings, while allies feel a strange loyalty, a desire to please her.

special_skills.name: Garden of Desires
special_skills.description: Forfota raises the Mirror of Longing and turns it in a slow circle. All who see their reflection in it are transported into a vision of their deepest desires, living out their fantasies in perfect detail. They are completely lost to the world, helpless as they pursue phantom happiness.

special_skills.name: Covetous Swarm
special_skills.description: She opens one of her pouches and releases a cloud of stolen desires—shimmering, formless motes of sapphire light. Each mote seeks out a target and attempts to enter them, filling them with a random, uncontrollable desire that distracts and disorients them.

special_skills.name: Serpent's Mirror
special_skills.description: Forfota coils her tail around herself and holds the Mirror of Longing before her face. The mirror reflects not her image, but the image of whatever her enemy most desires to see. As they stare, captivated, she slithers behind them, the Serpent's Fang ready.

ultimate_skill.name: Envy's Judgment: The Mirror of Infinite Want
ultimate_skill.description: Forfota Luigena's sapphire eyes blaze with the light of a thousand unfulfilled desires, and she rises up, her serpent body coiling beneath her, her vestigial wings fluttering rapidly. She holds the Mirror of Longing before her and speaks a single word: 'Want.' The mirror expands, growing to immense size, its frame twisting into an elaborate archway, its glass now a swirling vortex of sapphire light. From the mirror, a wave of pure, concentrated longing pours forth, washing over the battlefield. Every enemy is suddenly flooded with every desire they have ever had, all at once, magnified a thousandfold. They want everything—power, love, wealth, beauty, revenge, peace—and they want it now, with an intensity that shatters their ability to think, to move, to fight. They are paralyzed by the sheer overwhelming force of their own wants. While they are trapped in their infinite desire, Forfota moves among them, her serpent body flowing gracefully. With the Serpent's Fang, she makes a single, delicate cut on each one, injecting a venom that does not kill but locks them in this state of eternal wanting. They become living statues of desire, forever reaching for something they can never grasp. When the vision fades, the enemies are still standing, but their eyes are empty, their minds lost in an infinite loop of longing. Forfota coils in the center, the Mirror of Longing now returned to its normal size, held against her chest. She looks at the hollow shells around her and feels... nothing. The longing remains, as strong as ever. She is Forfota Luigena. She is Envy. And she still wants more.

title: Lust • The Rose-Tailed Demon
lore: In the pleasure districts of ancient Heian-kyo, where cherry blossoms fell like snow and the boundaries between dream and reality blurred with sake and incense, there lived a man named Hijyogen Sensi. He was a poet, a musician, a lover—a man of such extraordinary charm and beauty that nobles and commoners alike fell under his spell. But Hijyogen's gifts were also his curse. He loved deeply, truly, and was loved in return, but love was never enough. He wanted more—more passion, more beauty, more connection, more of everything. He would love a woman completely, then grow restless and move on, leaving a trail of broken hearts behind him. He did not mean to hurt them; he simply could not help himself. The hunger for new love, new beauty, new experience was a fire that never died. One night, he met a woman unlike any other. She was a noble's daughter, beautiful beyond words, and for the first time, Hijyogen thought he had found the one who could satisfy him. They spent a week together, a perfect dream of passion and poetry. But on the seventh night, she revealed herself to be a demon in disguise, sent by a rival who was jealous of Hijyogen's success. She laughed at him, told him that his love was a sickness, that he would never be satisfied, that he was as empty as the poems he wrote. She vanished, leaving him alone and shattered. He realized she was right. He was empty. He could love and love and love, but it would never fill the void. In his despair, he called out to any power that would listen, offering anything for the ability to feel complete, to be satisfied, to finally have enough. Vergasuis appeared, lounging on a silk cushion as if he had always been there. He offered Hijyogen a deal: become Lust itself, a being who could inspire desire in all who saw him, who could experience pleasure beyond mortal comprehension, in exchange for eternal service. Hijyogen accepted. His body transformed, becoming more beautiful than ever, but with monstrous additions. His skin took on a warm, pinkish-brown glow, smooth as silk. From his lower back, three long, prehensile tails emerged, each ending in a heart-shaped tuft of pink fur, covered in thousands of tiny sensory hairs that could feel the desires of others. Small, curved horns grew from his temples, the color of dark rosewood. His eyes became large, luminous pools of deep pink, with the power to inspire uncontrollable desire. But his face remained human—more beautiful than ever, with full lips and high cheekbones. He is Hijyogen Sensi, and he is loved by all, but loves none.
description: Hijyogen Sensi is the embodiment of irresistible desire and heartbreaking beauty, a being who inspires longing in all who behold him. He stands at a graceful five feet ten inches, his form lean and elegant, every movement a study in seduction. His skin is a warm, pinkish-brown, smooth as the finest silk, with a subtle luminescence that catches light and makes him seem to glow from within. His face is the epitome of male beauty—high, elegant cheekbones, a straight, refined nose, full lips always curved in a knowing, slightly sad smile, and a strong, defined jaw. But his eyes are his most devastating feature: they are large, luminous, and the color of deep rose pink, with vertical slit pupils like a cat's, holding an eternal, gentle hunger that makes those who meet his gaze feel seen, desired, wanted. They seem to promise that they understand your deepest longings. His hair is a magnificent mane of deep, rich brown, almost black, with streaks of rose pink that catch the light, falling past his shoulders in soft, flowing waves, often adorned with small pink flowers or silk cords. From his temples, two small, elegant horns curve back, the color of dark rosewood, polished and smooth, adding to his demonic beauty without diminishing his handsomeness. His most distinctive feature is his three tails. From his lower back, just above his hips, three long, prehensile tails emerge, each as thick as a rope and nearly six feet long, covered in the same warm pinkish-brown skin at the base, fading to soft, fluffy pink fur at the tips. Each tail ends in a heart-shaped tuft of that impossibly soft fur, and the entire length of the tails is covered in thousands of tiny, sensitive hairs that can feel the emotions and desires of those around him. The tails move constantly, flowing and curling with a life of their own, caressing the air, reaching out to touch, to feel, to inspire. His attire is that of a Heian-era noble, but rendered in sensual, luxurious fabrics. He wears a flowing silk robe of deep rose pink, embroidered with gold and silver thread in patterns of cherry blossoms and lovers embracing. The robe is open at the chest, revealing his smooth, hairless skin. Over this, he wears a shorter outer robe of black silk, embroidered with pink rose motifs, tied with a wide sash of deep burgundy. Around his neck, he wears a simple but elegant necklace of rose gold, with a single, teardrop pink gem resting at his throat. On his fingers, he wears several rings—rose gold set with pink gems, each one a gift from a lover now forgotten. In his hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Lover's Lute and the Thorned Whip. The Lover's Lute is an exquisite instrument carved from pale rosewood, inlaid with mother-of-pearl and pink gems, its strings made of spun silk and moonlight. Its music can inspire love, desire, and longing in all who hear it, or shatter hearts with its absence. The Thorned Whip is a delicate but deadly weapon, a long, slender whip braided from rose-pink leather, lined with tiny, curved thorns that leave wounds that ache with unfulfilled desire. He moves with a flowing, sensual grace, his tails swaying behind him, his eyes promising everything and delivering nothing. He is Hijyogen Sensi, and he is the dream you will never forget.

story.part1: Hijyogen's childhood was one of beauty and privilege. His father was a minor noble, his mother a famous courtesan, and he inherited the best of both worlds—status and sensuality. He learned music, poetry, and the art of love before he learned to read.
story.part2: By sixteen, he had broken his first heart. By twenty, he had lost count. He did not mean to hurt them; he simply could not stop. Each new love was a new world to explore, and he was an explorer at heart.
story.part3: He began to realize that something was wrong. He would love completely, passionately, then wake up one morning and feel nothing. The void inside him never filled, no matter how much love he poured into it.
story.part4: The demon woman was different. She matched him, desire for desire, passion for passion. For one week, he thought he had found his equal, his completion. When she revealed herself and mocked him, the void swallowed him whole.
story.part5: 'You are empty,' she said. 'You will always be empty.' He knew she was right. On the bridge overlooking the koi pond, he prepared to end it all. Vergasuis found him there.
story.part6: The demon king offered him a deal: become the embodiment of desire itself, and he would never want again—because he would be the want. He accepted, and his body transformed into something that inspired longing in all who saw him.
story.part7: Now, Hijyogen rules his domain, a palace of sensual pleasures where dreams and reality blur. He is loved by all who enter, but he loves none. His three tails feel the desires of everyone around him, and he uses that knowledge to give them what they want, but he feels nothing himself. He is the ultimate lover, and he is utterly, completely alone.

weapon.name: Lover's Lute
weapon.aura: The lute glows with a soft, pink light, and the air around it shimmers with barely visible rose-colored waves of sound. Its music is audible only to those it is meant for.
weapon.special_feature: The Lover's Lute is an exquisite instrument carved from pale rosewood, inlaid with mother-of-pearl and pink gems that pulse with inner light. Its strings are made not of gut or silk, but of spun moonlight and woven desire, and they resonate with the emotions of all who hear them. When Hijyogen plays, the music does not just please the ear; it speaks directly to the heart. A simple melody can inspire love in the coldest soul. A complex harmony can make an enemy forget their hatred and long only for peace. A single, discordant note can shatter a heart, leaving the victim broken with unrequited longing. The lute can also be used defensively, creating barriers of sound or disorienting enemies with overwhelming emotion.

The thorns are coated with a venom that does not kill; instead, it makes the victim experience an unbearable, unfulfilled longing for whatever they most desire. A lash from the whip leaves a wound that aches with desire, distracting and weakening the victim. The whip can also be used to entangle, caress, or disarm, its touch always leaving behind a lingering sense of want.

special_skills.name: Garden of Flesh

All who hear the music and see the tails are transported into a shared dream of sensual pleasure, their deepest desires played out in perfect detail. They are completely lost to the world, helpless in their own fantasies.

special_skills.name: Heartbreak Cascade
special_skills.description: He plays a series of sharp, discordant notes on the lute, each one aimed at a different enemy. Each note strikes like a physical blow, but instead of pain, it delivers a wave of heartbreak, of love lost, of desire unfulfilled. Enemies are left weeping, their will to fight shattered by overwhelming sadness.

special_skills.name: Thorned Embrace
special_skills.description: Hijyogen's three tails lash out simultaneously, wrapping around an enemy while his whip coils around another. The tails caress and soothe while the whip's thorns prick and ache, creating a confusing mixture of pleasure and pain that leaves the target utterly disoriented and helpless.

ultimate_skill.name: Lust's Judgment: The Eternal Embrace
ultimate_skill.description: Hijyogen Sensi's pink eyes blaze with the light of a thousand lovers' sighs, and his three tails fan out behind him, their heart-shaped tips glowing with intense pink light. He begins to play the Lover's Lute, but the music is not heard; it is felt, a vibration that resonates in the very souls of all who witness it. The melody is the song of every lover who has ever lived, every moment of passion, every sigh of contentment, every tear of heartbreak. It is the sound of desire itself. As the music plays, his tails extend, growing longer and longer, their pink fur shimmering, until they envelop the entire battlefield in a soft, glowing cocoon of pink light. Within this cocoon, every enemy experiences their ultimate desire—not as a vision, but as reality. They live their perfect moment, their greatest fantasy, in exquisite, heartbreaking detail. They are loved as they have always wanted to be loved. They have what they have always wanted. And it is perfect. But perfection cannot last. As the moment reaches its peak, Hijyogen plays a single, final note—a note of farewell, of loss, of inevitable heartbreak. The fantasy shatters. The enemies are left with the memory of perfect love, now gone forever, an ache that will never heal. They fall to their knees, not wounded, but broken by loss. The pink cocoon fades, and Hijyogen stands at the center, his tails slowly retracting, his eyes dim. He looks at the broken forms around him, and for a moment, his sad smile is genuine. He has given them what they wanted, and taken it away. It is the only gift he has to give. He is Hijyogen Sensi. He is Lust. And he is still alone.

title: Gluttony • The Emerald Toad
lore: In a small farming village in ancient Thailand, there lived a boy named Tetilan Murgasta who was always hungry. Not for food alone, but for everything. He wanted more rice, more fish, more stories, more warmth, more life. His family was poor, and there was never enough. He watched his siblings go to bed hungry so that he could eat, and the hunger twisted into something else—a desperate, gnawing need to consume, to fill the void, to never be empty again. As he grew, so did his hunger. He ate everything he could find, then began to collect things—rocks, sticks, insects, anything to fill his pockets, his room, his soul. He married a woman who loved him, but his hunger consumed their marriage. He had children, but his hunger consumed his attention. He was never satisfied, never full, never enough. One day, a famine came to the village. The rice paddies dried up, the fish died, the animals starved. Tetilan watched his children grow thin, his wife grow weak, and the hunger inside him became a monster. He began to hoard the little food that remained, hiding it from his own family, eating in secret while they starved. When his wife caught him, her look of betrayal was worse than any wound. She took the children and left, and Tetilan was alone with his hunger. In his despair, he called out to any power that would listen, offering anything to never be hungry again, to finally be full. Vergasuis appeared, sitting on a pile of bones, and offered him a deal: become Gluttony itself, a being who could consume endlessly, who would never be empty, in exchange for eternal service. Tetilan accepted. His body swelled and transformed, becoming massive and toad-like. His skin took on a deep, mottled green and black, with warts that oozed a red, hungry slime. His mouth widened, filled with rows of teeth, and his tongue became a long, prehensile weapon. But his face remained human—a strange, sad contrast to his monstrous body, with warm brown eyes that still held the ghost of the man he had been. He is Tetilan Murgasta, and he is always, always hungry.
description: Tetilan Murgasta is a monument to consumption, a massive, toad-like being whose hunger is written in every line of his form. He stands—or rather, squats—at an immense seven feet tall in his human upper body, but his overall bulk makes him seem much larger. From the waist up, he is human in shape, but swollen and oversized, his torso thick and powerful, his arms massive and corded with muscle. His skin is a deep, mottled green with black patches, rough and warty, each wart oozing a thin, red slime that is actually concentrated digestive fluid, hungry to consume. His face is a shocking contrast to his monstrous body: it is human, and strangely handsome, with warm, dark brown eyes that hold an eternal, sad hunger, full lips, and high cheekbones. His expression is one of perpetual, mournful longing, as if he is always remembering what it felt like to be satisfied. His hair is black, shot through with streaks of green, pulled back into a messy knot at the nape of his neck. From the waist down, he is pure toad—massive, powerful legs built for leaping, their skin the same mottled green and black, ending in wide, webbed feet with sharp claws. His most distinctive feature is his mouth and tongue. His mouth is enormous, stretching from ear to ear when fully opened, filled with multiple rows of sharp, pointed teeth designed for grinding and swallowing. His tongue is a prehensile weapon, nearly twenty feet long, deep red and covered in sticky, digestive slime, able to lash out and snatch prey from a distance. On his back, clusters of large, green-black warts pulse and glow with a faint, red light when he is hungry—which is always. His attire is minimal, as his body needs little covering. He wears a loose, open vest of dark green fabric, embroidered with red thread in patterns of consuming flames and endless feasts, barely containing his massive torso. A wide belt of red leather cinches his waist, from which hang numerous pouches and containers, each holding something he has consumed and preserved—a memory, a soul, a moment of satisfaction. Around his neck, he wears a necklace of bones and teeth, trophies of things he has devoured. In his massive hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Maw Opener and the Feast Bringer. The Maw Opener is a massive, two-handed cleaver, its blade forged from a single piece of meteoric iron, its edge gleaming with a hungry red light, able to carve through anything. The Feast Bringer is an enormous, ornate ladle, carved from bone and inlaid with jade and red gems, capable of scooping up souls and serving them for consumption. He moves with a deceptive speed, his powerful legs allowing him to leap great distances, his tongue lashing out, his cleaver swinging. He is Tetilan Murgasta, and he is never full.

story.part1: Tetilan's earliest memories are of hunger. Not the simple hunger of a missed meal, but the deep, existential hunger of never having enough. He watched his siblings starve so he could eat, and the guilt mixed with the hunger into a poison that would never leave him.
story.part2: He began to hoard as a child—food, then rocks, then anything he could find. The hoarding made him feel safe, full, but the feeling never lasted. He always needed more.
story.part3: He married a woman who loved him despite his hunger. She tried to fill the void with her love, and for a while, it worked. But the hunger always returned, stronger than before.
story.part4: When the famine came, the hunger became a monster. He watched his children grow thin and did nothing. He hoarded food, ate in secret, lied to his wife. When she caught him, the look in her eyes was the worst thing he had ever seen.
story.part5: She left, taking the children. He was alone with his hunger, and it was all he had left. He called out to any power that would listen, offering everything for the ability to finally be full.
story.part6: Vergasuis appeared and offered him a deal: become Gluttony, and he would never be empty again. He would consume endlessly, and the consumption itself would be his satisfaction. He accepted.
story.part7: Now, Tetilan rules his domain, a vast, ever-expanding feast hall where he consumes everything—food, souls, memories, worlds. But the hunger never stops. It never will. He is Tetilan Murgasta, and he is always, always hungry.

basic_skills.name: Hungry Gaze
basic_skills.description: Tetilan fixes his sad, hungry eyes on a target. The target feels a sudden, inexplicable hunger, a gnawing emptiness that distracts them and makes them vulnerable.

basic_skills.name: Tongue Lash
basic_skills.description: His twenty-foot tongue lashes out, striking a target from a distance. The tongue wraps around them, its sticky slime holding them fast, and begins to drag them toward his waiting mouth.

basic_skills.name: Consuming Cleave
basic_skills.description: He swings the Maw Opener in a powerful arc, carving through multiple enemies or obstacles. The blade leaves trails of red light, and the wounded bleed life force that Tetilan absorbs.

passive_skill.name: Eternal Hunger
passive_skill.description: Tetilan is perpetually hungry, and this hunger fuels his power. The hungrier he is, the stronger, faster, and more durable he becomes. His hunger is bottomless, so his power has no theoretical limit. Additionally, his presence inspires hunger in others, making them crave food, power, or satisfaction, distracting them and making them susceptible to his offers of 'feasts.'

special_skills.name: Feast of Souls
special_skills.description: Tetilan raises the Feast Bringer and scoops up the souls of recently fallen enemies—or living ones, if they are close enough. He consumes them, adding their power to his own and healing his wounds. The souls scream as they are swallowed, a sound that terrifies other enemies.

special_skills.name: Hungry Maw
special_skills.description: Tetilan opens his mouth impossibly wide, revealing the endless, dark void of his hunger. A powerful vacuum pulls all enemies and objects toward him, drawing them into his waiting jaws. Those caught are consumed, their power added to his.

special_skills.name: Consuming Leap
special_skills.description: His powerful toad legs launch him into the air, and he comes crashing down on an enemy, his massive bulk crushing them while his Maw Opener swings and his tongue lashes out, consuming everything in reach.

ultimate_skill.name: Gluttony's Judgment: The Endless Feast
ultimate_skill.description: Tetilan Murgasta's sad, hungry eyes blaze with red light, and his entire body begins to pulse and swell. The warts on his back glow brighter, oozing rivers of digestive slime. He opens his mouth wider than should be possible, wider than physically possible, revealing not a throat, but a void, an endless darkness that leads to his infinite hunger. He raises both the Maw Opener and the Feast Bringer and speaks a single, guttural word: 'Feast.' In that moment, the battlefield becomes his dining hall. The Maw Opener swings in massive arcs, carving through everything—enemies, terrain, magic—and each cut releases life force that flows into his open mouth. The Feast Bringer scoops up entire groups of enemies, pouring them into the void. His tongue lashes out in a dozen directions at once, each tip somehow splitting, grabbing, dragging. And at the center of it all, Tetilan's mouth is an event horizon, pulling everything toward it. Enemies who resist the pull find themselves slowly, inexorably sliding toward the void, their feet leaving trails in the earth. When the feast finally ends, when the last enemy has been consumed, Tetilan's mouth slowly closes. He belches, a cloud of red and green smoke, and his eyes return to their sad, hungry brown. He is not full. He will never be full. But for a moment, the hunger is... quieter. He looks at the empty battlefield, at the places where enemies once stood, and his expression is one of profound, eternal sadness. He is Tetilan Murgasta. He is Gluttony. And the feast is never over.

title: Sloth • The Violet Sloth
lore: In a small village in the mountains of Nepal, there lived a man named Umestra Felondra who was tired. Not just physically tired, but soul-tired. He had been born into a family of farmers, and from the moment he could walk, he worked. He worked in the fields, in the house, in the village. He worked until his hands bled and his back ached and his spirit was ground to dust. He watched his father work himself to death, watched his mother follow soon after, and he knew that the same fate awaited him. There was no escape. There was no rest. There was only work, until you died. He began to slow down. Not deliberately at first, but because his body and soul simply could not keep up. He moved slower, spoke slower, thought slower. The other villagers mocked him, called him lazy, called him worthless. But they did not understand. It was not laziness; it was despair. He had given up. One day, a landslide destroyed the village's fields, wiping out their entire harvest. While the other villagers scrambled to rebuild, to salvage, to survive, Umestra simply sat down. He sat down and watched them, feeling nothing. He was too tired to care, too tired to move, too tired to even be afraid. As night fell and the villagers wept and worked, Vergasuis appeared beside him, sitting on a rock as if he had always been there. 'You are tired,' the demon king said. 'Tired of working, tired of struggling, tired of trying. I can give you rest. Eternal rest. In exchange for your service.' Umestra looked at him with his heavy-lidded eyes and asked, 'Will I have to work?' Vergasuis laughed. 'No. You will never have to work again. You will simply be. You will become Sloth itself, and the world will slow down around you.' Umestra accepted. His body transformed, becoming soft and round, his skin taking on a deep violet-grey, his limbs elongating into the shape of a sloth's. His movements became impossibly slow, but his perception of time shifted so that the world seemed to move at a normal pace. He could think, dream, exist, without ever having to move. His face remained human—handsome in a soft, gentle way, with heavy-lidded eyes that always seemed half-asleep, and a peaceful, content smile. He is Umestra Felondra, and he has finally found rest.
description: Umestra Felondra is the embodiment of eternal rest and infinite patience, a being who has transcended the need for movement. He hangs, more often than not, suspended from a massive, ancient tree in his domain, his body designed for perfect stillness. From the waist up, he is human in shape, but soft and rounded, with a gentle, peaceful quality. His skin is a deep violet-grey, smooth and soft to the touch, with a faint, subtle luminescence. His face is handsome in a soft, gentle way—high cheekbones, a straight nose, full lips always curved in a peaceful, content smile, and heavy-lidded eyes that seem perpetually half-asleep. His eyes are large and a deep, calm purple, with no visible pupils, holding an eternal, dreamy peace that is both comforting and unsettling. His hair is a soft, silvery-grey, almost white, cut short and fluffy, like the fur of a sloth. From his shoulders and down his back, a thick, soft coat of violet-grey fur covers him, warm and insulating. His arms are long and elegant, ending in three-fingered hands with long, curved claws designed for gripping branches. His legs are similarly long and curled, ending in three-toed feet with the same curved claws. His entire body is designed for hanging, for stillness, for waiting. He moves with excruciating slowness when he moves at all, but his perception of time is so altered that the world seems to move at a normal pace to him. His attire is minimal—a soft, draped garment of deep purple silk, wrapped around his lower body and over one shoulder, providing modesty without restricting his hanging posture. Around his neck, he wears a simple necklace of polished lavender stones, each one a dream he has captured and preserved. On his back, he carries his legendary weapons: the Dream Catcher and the Stillness Spear. The Dream Catcher is an ornate, circular frame of twisted silver and purple wood, woven with a web of soft, violet threads that shimmer with captured dreams. It can catch, store, and release dreams, and those caught in its web fall into an endless sleep. The Stillness Spear is a long, elegant spear with a shaft of pale grey wood and a head of polished purple crystal, designed to be thrown or thrust with devastating precision, freezing whatever it touches in a state of perfect stillness. He hangs from his tree, dreaming eternally, and those who disturb his rest find themselves joining him in sleep.

story.part1: Umestra's childhood was one of endless labor. He worked before dawn and after dusk, his body aching, his spirit slowly dying. He watched his parents work themselves to death, and he knew his fate was the same.
story.part2: He began to slow down as a young man, not out of laziness, but out of despair. What was the point of hurrying toward death? He moved slower, spoke slower, thought slower, and the village mocked him.
story.part3: He tried to explain, to tell them that he was tired, not lazy, but they did not listen. They called him worthless, a burden, a waste of space. He stopped trying to explain. He stopped trying at all.
story.part4: When the landslide destroyed the fields, he simply sat down. He watched the others scramble and struggle, and he felt nothing. He was too tired to care, too tired to move, too tired to even be afraid.
story.part5: As night fell, Vergasuis appeared. The demon king offered him eternal rest, an end to all struggle, in exchange for his service. Umestra asked only one question: 'Will I have to work?'
story.part6: When Vergasuis said no, Umestra accepted without hesitation. His body transformed into something designed for perfect stillness, and he felt, for the first time in his life, peace.
story.part7: Now, Umestra hangs from his ancient tree, dreaming eternally. He does not rule his domain so much as inhabit it, a peaceful presence in a realm of stillness. Those who enter his domain often find themselves slowing down, growing sleepy, until they too hang from branches, dreaming. He is Umestra Felondra, and he has finally found rest.

special_skills.description: Umestra raises the Dream Catcher and spins it slowly.
