special_skills.name: Eternal Nap
special_skills.description: Umestra wraps his long arms and legs around a target, holding them in a gentle, inescapable embrace. As he holds them, his aura of stillness and sleep transfers to them, and they slowly, peacefully, fall into an endless sleep in his arms.

ultimate_skill.name: Sloth's Judgment: The Endless Dream
ultimate_skill.description: Umestra Felondra's calm purple eyes open fully for the first time, and they blaze with a soft, peaceful light. He raises the Dream Catcher high, and its web expands, growing to immense size, its violet threads spreading across the entire battlefield like a giant spider's web. He then throws the Stillness Spear into the center of the web, and the spear's power radiates through every strand. In that moment, the battlefield becomes a dream. Every enemy is caught in the web, not physically, but mentally. They are pulled into their own personal dream, a perfect, peaceful fantasy where all their desires are fulfilled, all their struggles ended. They are content. They are happy. They never want to leave. And they don't. They simply hang there, suspended in the web, dreaming eternally, their faces peaceful, their bodies still. Umestra watches them for a moment, then slowly, gently, begins to pull the web closed, gathering the dreamers together. He will keep them safe, keep them dreaming, keep them at peace. They will never have to work again. They will never struggle again. They will simply be. He settles back into his hanging posture, the web gathered around him, the spear resting at his side, and his eyes slowly close, returning to their half-asleep state. He is Umestra Felondra. He is Sloth. And finally, everyone can rest.

title: The Obsidian Throne, King of Demons
nickname: He Who Grants Desires and Collects Souls
lore: Before the first sin was committed, before the first mortal soul was forged, there was Vergasuis Motred. He was not born; he coalesced from the primordial darkness that existed before light, from the void where even the gods feared to tread. He is the original, the first demon, the source from which all demonic power flows. For eons beyond counting, he existed in solitude, watching the universe take shape, watching the gods create their mortals, watching the mortals stumble and fall. He was patient, for he had eternity. He waited for the moment when mortals would be ready, when their desires would be strong enough, their wills weak enough, their souls ripe for the taking. That moment came when the first human looked at what another had and felt the sting of want. Vergasuis appeared to that human, a shadow with eyes like dying stars, and made his first offer: a desire fulfilled, in exchange for a soul. The human accepted. And Vergasuis tasted his first soul, a flavor more exquisite than anything in creation. He was hooked. Over the millennia, Vergasuis has collected countless souls, each one a unique flavor, a unique story, a unique addition to his endless hoard. He does not conquer; he does not wage war. He waits, and he offers. He is the ultimate tempter, the cosmic dealer in desires, the king who sits on a throne of skulls and watches the parade of the damned. He created the seven deadly sins not as servants, but as extensions of his will, embodiments of the very desires he exploits. Each sin was once a human who, in their moment of greatest despair or desire, cried out for power. Vergasuis answered, transformed them, and bound them to himself. They are his children, his tools, his entertainment. He watches them scheme against each other, compete for his favor, struggle for power, and he is amused. For he knows that no matter how powerful they become, they are still his, their souls still his, their desires still his to exploit. He is Vergasuis Motred, and he is patient. He will wait for you too.
description: Vergasuis Motred is the embodiment of absolute, ancient evil, a being of such overwhelming presence that the very air around him seems to darken and still. He stands at an imposing seven feet six inches, his frame broad and powerful, built like a conqueror, like a king who has never needed to lift a weapon because his will alone is enough. His physique is that of a perfect warrior-king—broad shoulders, a deep chest, powerful arms and legs—but there is a stillness to him, a patience that is more terrifying than any aggression. His skin is the color of dark, polished obsidian, smooth and flawless, with a faint, almost imperceptible shimmer, as if the void of space itself has been given form. It is cool to the touch, like stone that has never known sunlight. His face is a study in terrifying grace. It is human, and astonishingly handsome, with features that are almost too perfect—high, aristocratic cheekbones, a strong, straight nose, a firm, sculpted jaw, and full lips that are usually curved in a slight, knowing smile that promises nothing good. His brows are sharp and arch slightly, giving him a perpetually amused, calculating expression. But his eyes are the true windows to his ancient, malevolent soul. They are large, deep-set, and the color of dying stars—a swirling, hypnotic mix of deep violet, blood red, and absolute black, with no visible pupils, just cosmic chaos held in twin orbs. They seem to contain galaxies being born and dying, souls screaming in eternal torment, and the cold, patient amusement of a being who has seen it all and found it wanting. When he focuses on you, you feel the weight of eternity pressing down, and you know that every secret, every desire, every fear you have ever had is laid bare before him. His hair is a magnificent mane of deep, midnight black, so dark it absorbs light, falling past his shoulders in thick, straight waves, with subtle streaks of deep violet and crimson that only visible when they catch the light. It is immaculately groomed, a king's hair, often pulled back from his face with golden or obsidian clasps. From his brow, a magnificent crown of seven curved horns rises, each one representing one of the seven deadly sins. The horns are polished obsidian with veins of gold, each one uniquely shaped: one curves like a peacock feather for Pride, one is segmented like a centipede for Greed, one twists like a scorpion's tail for Wrath, one coils like a serpent for Envy, one curls like a ram's for Lust, one is thick and blunt for Gluttony, and one hangs heavy and drooping for Sloth. The crown of horns frames his face, giving him an aura of terrible, absolute authority. His attire is a magnificent fusion of imperial demonic armor and royal robes. He wears a cuirass of polished obsidian plates, etched with glowing red and violet runes that pulse with inner light, the armor shaped to his powerful torso, with golden trim at the edges. Over this, he wears a flowing robe of deep violet silk, embroidered with gold and silver thread in patterns of souls ascending and descending, of cosmic scales weighing hearts, of the seven sins dancing. The robe is open at the front, revealing the armor beneath, and drapes over his broad shoulders, falling to his feet. A massive, fur-trimmed cloak of black velvet, lined with deep crimson silk, hangs from his shoulders, the fur as black as midnight, adding to his imposing silhouette. Around his waist, a wide belt of hammered gold, set with seven massive gems—orange, yellow, red, blue, pink, green, and purple—each one representing a sin, each one pulsing with inner light. On his hands, he wears gauntlets of obsidian and gold, the fingers articulated, the knuckles set with smaller versions of the seven gems. On his head, in addition to the horned crown, he wears a simple but elegant circlet of gold, set with a single, massive black diamond at his brow. On his feet, he wears boots of obsidian plate and gold, their heels clicking with authority. In his hands, he carries his legendary weapons: the Sceptre of Desires and the Blade of Final Offers. The Sceptre of Desires is a tall, ornate staff of black obsidian, topped with a massive, faceted gem that swirls with the colors of all seven sins—a hypnotic, ever-changing light show. The sceptre can grant desires, but always at a terrible cost. The Blade of Final Offers is a massive, two-handed greatsword, its blade forged from the same obsidian as his armor, its edge impossibly sharp, its surface etched with the names of every soul he has ever collected, the names glowing with red light. He carries them not as tools of combat, but as symbols of his office, as instruments of his deals. He moves with a slow, deliberate grace, each step measured and eternal, his presence filling any space he occupies, making it feel smaller, darker, heavier. He is Vergasuis Motred, and he is waiting.

story.part1: Vergasuis does not have a beginning in the way mortals understand it. He simply was, a consciousness in the primordial void, watching light and matter coalesce, watching the first gods take form, watching them create. He felt no jealousy, no anger, only curiosity. He watched, and he waited.
story.part2: When the first mortals were created, he was fascinated. These tiny, fragile beings, with their brief lives and burning desires—they were so different from the eternal, passionless gods. He watched them love, hate, want, despair. He saw that their desires were their greatest strength and their greatest weakness.
story.part3: The first offer was made to a woman in ancient Mesopotamia who wanted her dead son back. Vergasuis appeared to her, offered to return the boy in exchange for her soul. She agreed, and he tasted his first soul. The flavor was exquisite—a complex blend of love, grief, hope, and despair. He knew then that he had found his purpose.
story.part4: Over the millennia, he collected millions of souls. He became a legend, a nightmare, a tempter. He learned to read desires like a book, to know exactly what each soul would pay, what each heart most wanted. He became patient, for he had eternity, and there would always be more souls.
story.part5: The creation of the seven sins was an experiment. He found mortals whose desires were so powerful, so all-consuming, that they could not be satisfied with a simple trade. He offered them transformation, made them embodiments of their own desires, bound them to himself. They became his children, his generals, his entertainment.
story.part6: He watches them now, the seven sins, as they scheme and compete for his favor. He finds it amusing, like watching children play at power. They do not realize that they are still his, that their souls are still his, that their desires are still his to exploit. He lets them believe they are free. It makes the game more interesting.
story.part7: Now, Vergasuis sits on his Obsidian Throne, in his domain between worlds, and he waits. He is patient. He will always be patient. He watches the mortal realm, sees their desires, their needs, their weaknesses. And he knows that, eventually, they will call out to him. They always do. He is Vergasuis Motred, and he is waiting for you.

weapon.special_feature: The Sceptre of Desires is a tall, ornate staff of black obsidian, taller than Vergasuis himself, topped with a massive, faceted gem that swirls with the colors of all seven sins in an ever-changing, hypnotic display. The staff is carved with images of souls ascending and descending, of deals being made, of desires being fulfilled and cursed. The sceptre is the physical manifestation of Vergasuis's power over desire. With it, he can grant any desire—but always at a cost, always with a twist, always binding the recipient to him. He can also use it to read desires from a distance, to manipulate them, to amplify them until they consume the one who holds them. In combat, the sceptre can unleash waves of pure desire energy, overwhelming enemies with their own wants, or create barriers of solidified longing.
special_skills: Desire Grant (fulfills a wish at a terrible cost)
Desire Reading (sees the deepest wants of any target)
Desire Wave (unleashes a wave of pure want, overwhelming enemies)
Desire Barrier (creates a wall of solidified longing)

weapon.name: Blade of Final Offers
weapon.aura: The blade glows with a deep, blood red light, and the names etched on its surface pulse and shift, new ones appearing as souls are collected. The air around it is cold, the temperature dropping noticeably near the blade.
weapon.special_feature: The Blade of Final Offers is a massive, two-handed greatsword, its blade forged from the same obsidian as Vergasuis's armor, impossibly black, yet somehow gleaming. The edge is impossibly sharp, able to cut through anything—flesh, stone, magic, even souls. The blade's surface is etched with the names of every soul Vergasuis has ever collected, millions upon millions of names, each one glowing with red light, constantly shifting and rearranging as new names are added. The sword is not primarily a weapon of combat; it is an instrument of finality. When a deal is made, when a soul is forfeit, Vergasuis draws the blade and touches it to the soul, and the name is etched into the blade, the soul collected. In combat, the sword is devastating, each swing leaving a trail of red light, and any wound it inflicts not only damages the body but also cuts the soul, leaving a permanent mark that Vergasuis can use to track and claim the victim later.
special_skills: Soul Cut (wounds the soul as well as the body)
Name Etching (collects a soul, adding its name to the blade)
Soul Track (can track any soul he has wounded)
Final Swing (a devastating strike that can cut through anything)

basic_skills.name: Cosmic Gaze
basic_skills.description: Vergasuis fixes his swirling, dying-star eyes on a target. The weight of eternity, of millions of souls, of ancient evil, presses down on them, and they are paralyzed, their minds unable to comprehend what they are seeing, their secrets laid bare.

basic_skills.name: Desire Whisper
basic_skills.description: He speaks a single word, and that word is the target's deepest desire, whispered directly into their mind. The target is momentarily overwhelmed by the intensity of their own want, unable to focus on anything else.

basic_skills.name: Sceptre Tap
basic_skills.description: He taps the Sceptre of Desires on the ground, and a wave of colored energy expands outward. Enemies feel their desires rise up, distracting them, while allies (if he has any) feel their wants sharpen, their focus intensifying.

passive_skill.name: Aura of the Obsidian Throne
passive_skill.description: Vergasuis radiates an aura of absolute, ancient authority at all times. All who come near him feel the weight of his presence—mortals are often rendered speechless, their wills crumbling; lesser demons instinctively bow; even the seven sins feel a flicker of their original fear. This aura makes it nearly impossible to lie to him, to hide from him, or to act against him. He is the king, and all who enter his presence know it.

special_skills.name: Garden of Desires
special_skills.description: Vergasuis raises the Sceptre of Desires and unleashes its full power. The area around him transforms into a manifestation of every enemy's deepest desires, rendered in perfect, tempting detail. Enemies become lost in their own fantasies, chasing illusions while Vergasuis watches, amused.

special_skills.name: Soul Harvest
special_skills.description: He draws the Blade of Final Offers and swings it in a wide arc. The blade does not cut flesh; it cuts through the air, and from the spectral wound, the souls of those who have made deals with him—or those whose desires have consumed them—are drawn out, their names flying to etch themselves on the blade. The souls scream as they are collected.

special_skills.name: Final Offer
special_skills.description: Vergasuis fixes his gaze on a single target and speaks. He offers them exactly what they most desire—no tricks, no twists, a genuine offer. But the price is their soul, now and forever. The target must choose, and their choice, either way, reveals the true nature of their desire.

ultimate_skill.name: Demon King's Judgment: The Eternal Ledger
ultimate_skill.description: Vergasuis Motred's dying-star eyes blaze with the light of a thousand dying galaxies, and he raises both the Sceptre of Desires and the Blade of Final Offers high above his head. The seven gems on his belt flare with blinding light, each color representing a sin, and behind him, the spectral forms of the seven deadly sins appear—Seseei, Kukiun, Gehani, Forfota, Hijyogen, Tetilan, and Umestra—their powers flowing into him. He speaks a single word: 'Render.' In that moment, the battlefield becomes a cosmic ledger. Every soul present is laid bare, their every desire, every sin, every secret written in lines of fire before them. The Blade of Final Offers swings in a slow, majestic arc, and as it passes, the names of those whose desires have condemned them are carved into the air before being absorbed into the blade. The Sceptre of Desires pulses, and those whose desires are pure, whose wants are selfless, are spared, but those whose desires are selfish, cruel, or destructive find their wants amplified to the point of madness, consuming them from within. The seven sins circle the battlefield, each claiming those who embody their domain. When the judgment ends, the battlefield is transformed. The worthy are left standing, shaken but alive. The unworthy are gone—their souls added to the blade, their names etched for eternity. The sins fade back into the shadows. Vergasuis lowers his weapons, his eyes slowly dimming, and surveys the scene with that slight, knowing smile. He has collected another harvest. He has judged another batch of souls. He is Vergasuis Motred, the Demon King, and the ledger is never closed.
